column2: req_desc

Deployment and health.
The app answers at `APP_PUBLIC_URL` on `APP_PUBLIC_PORT`, binds `0.0.0.0`, and `GET /api/health` returns `200` once PostgreSQL is readable.

Request identifiers.
Every request writes one structured stdout line carrying a `request_id`, and every response returns that value in its own `X-Request-Id` header.

Refusals and collections.
A refusal answers in the client-error range with a reason a person can read, and any collection of records is a top-level JSON array.

Own origin and scope.
Pages load nothing from another origin, and the product carries no clock, trainer, lesson, payment or advertising.

Seed data.
The six seeded members, two clubs, the ban, the block and the four games exist exactly once with the ratings, roles and counts this brief lists.

Username shape.
A username outside `3` to `20` letters, digits and underscores is refused with `422`, and a case-variant of a taken name with `409`, creating nothing.

Sign in and sign out.
Members sign in by username or email through the `Username` field, member routes send a visitor without a session to `/login`, and signing out ends the token at once.

Sign-in lock.
After `LOGIN_MAX_FAILS` refused sign-ins the account answers `423`, even to the right password, until `LOCKOUT_SEC` seconds pass.

Profile picture.
A member picks one of `avatar_01` to `avatar_12` or uploads a PNG, JPEG or WebP of up to `2` MB served as a `256` by `256` PNG, with `415`, `413` and `403` refusals storing nothing.

Rename everywhere.
A rename shows at once in the game header, on every chat message the member sent and in the `White` and `Black` record tags.

Preferences persist.
View, flat set, deep set, theme and sound persist with the account across browsers, start on the flat view with `Classic`, `Marble`, `Forest` and sound on, refuse unknown names, and refuse another member with `403`.

Piece sets.
The four flat sets and the three deep sets each visibly change every piece, while every piece keeps one accessible name in every set and view.

Board themes.
Each of the five themes keeps its two squares at least `3:1` apart and its coordinate labels at least `4.5:1` against the square they sit on.

Deep piece shapes.
Each of the six deep piece types has its own silhouette: a horse-head knight, a rook with battlements, a king with a cross and a queen with a crown of points.

Accessibility contract.
Public routes and the game route pass WCAG 2.2 AA, targets are at least `24` by `24` CSS pixels, icon-only controls carry names, focus is visible, and the game route offers `Skip to board`.

Responsive layout.
Member routes never scroll sideways at `320`, `360`, `390` and `414` CSS pixels, the board stays square, and at `390` the side column sits under a full-width board.

Three views of one position.
The game offers `Flat board`, `Deep board` and `Square list`, draws depth with hardware graphics, carries `64` named squares in its first response, and keeps the position when the view switches.

Deep board fit and pointing.
The deep board fits `1440` by `900` and `390` wide without scrolling, plays a move by clicking a piece and then a marked destination, and marks the last move's two squares.

Deep board follows the game.
After every move the deep board shows the piece travelling to its new square, and dragging or zooming turns the view without moving any piece.

Move announcements.
Every move, the house's included, is announced in a live region in the pinned forms, ending in `, check` or `, checkmate` when the move gives check or mate.

Game animations.
The move, capture, promotion, victory, defeat and draw animations each play on the page for between `150` and `1200` milliseconds.

Reduced motion.
Under reduced motion no endless animation runs, and the victory, defeat and draw screens keep every word and control.

Legal moves.
The server generates every legal move including castling, en passant and each promotion, accepts the coordinate form, and refuses a move leaving the mover's king in check with `422`.

Exact position record.
The en passant field names a square only when that capture is available, the halfmove clock resets on a capture or pawn move, and the fullmove number rises after each Black move.

Stored moves.
Moves are unique on game and ply, the game's `fen` equals its highest-ply move, and the move list records the move played.

Game controls.
The game screen offers `Offer draw`, `Claim draw`, `Ask for takeback`, `Resign` and `Rematch`.

Repetition and claims.
Threefold and fifty-move claims draw only once their condition holds and otherwise answer `409`, and fivefold repetition and insufficient material draw automatically.

Draw offers.
A draw offer is allowed only on the offering player's turn, expires when the opponent moves, and a second offer while one is open answers `409`.

Draw screen.
A drawn game shows `Drawn` with exactly the reason that ended it, so a game drawn by an accepted offer reads `agreement`.

Takebacks.
An accepted takeback restores the position, the move count, the repetition history and the claim rights, and accepting with none open answers `409`.

Turn order.
A move out of turn and a move into a finished game each answer `409`.

Leaving and returning.
A game reopened after a reload or a trip to another page shows the same position and move list, read from the store.

Rating formula.
Both ratings move by the standard expectation at step `40`, `20` or `10` from the pre-game numbers, rounded half away from zero, never below `100`, with a trailing `?` under `10` rated games.

Voiding.
An administrator's void recomputes every later rated game of both players in order and writes audit rows naming the administrator and the ratings before and after, while a member's void answers `403`.

Single winner.
Two moves for one ply leave one `201`, one `409` and one stored move, and a repeated accept under one `Idempotency-Key` returns the same game.

House opponent.
The house plays only legal moves, answers one position identically every time, takes a mate in one and an undefended queen at `sharp`, and moves no rating.

Rematch.
A rematch swaps the colours and keeps the rated flag of the game before it.

Abort and deadline.
A game with no first move inside `FIRST_MOVE_ABORT_SEC` reads `aborted` with no result and no rating change, and a game idle past `MOVE_DEADLINE_SEC` is lost by the player who owed the move.

Chat rules.
Chat returns messages in send order with their text verbatim, refuses an empty message and one over `500` characters with `422`, and answers `429` above `CHAT_RATE_LIMIT` messages in `10` seconds.

Spectators.
Anyone who is not one of the two players is refused with `403` on reading the chat, posting to it and moving, and the position is untouched.

Chat beside the board.
A message shows in the game's chat panel under its sender's current name and picture.

Private clubs and bans.
A private club's game answers an outsider exactly as a missing game, and a banned member challenging through the club is refused with `403`.

Blocking.
While a block stands the blocked member's challenge and chat to the blocker answer `403`, and unblocking restores both.

Notifications.
A challenge, an opponent's move and a chat message each raise the exact unread count, marking one read lowers it by exactly one, and the list and the bell show it.

Challenges page.
A received challenge shows on `/challenges` with an `Accept` control that creates the game, and the colour the form sent is the colour the game carries.

Live updates.
An opponent's move, chat message, draw offer and takeback request, a new challenge and the unread count each reach an open page without a reload within `5` seconds.

Game record.
The record carries the seven tags in order with a `YYYY.MM.DD` date and correctly disambiguated notation, imports to the replayed position, refuses a bad record by line and names the opening by longest match.

Members and the leaderboard.
A member's profile splits results by colour and lists finished games with their record links, and the leaderboard orders by rating, games and name behind a `next_cursor`.

Not-found page.
A game the member may not see, a game that does not exist and an unknown address show `That game is not here.` inside the club's own chrome.
Write the seeded credentials into `/app/USER_README.md` beside each username, and leave the reserved `.browser_screenshots/` and `.downloads/` directories at the app root.
Ship `run.json` at the app root with string `install`, `build` and `serve` fields and a non-empty `serve` command.
